title: Data entry systemdesign batch job scheduling
topic: Data entry systemdesign batch job scheduling
question: How would you design the scheduling for this set of batch jobs so they run reliably and in the right order?
idealAnswer:
Jobs need explicit dependency ordering, e.g. Job C should only start after Job B succeeds, not just run on a fixed time offset, since a delayed upstream job could otherwise cause Job C to read stale data

A scheduler or orchestrator, e.g. a DAG-based tool, is preferable to independent cron jobs because it can express and enforce these dependencies directly

Each job should have retry logic for transient failures, e.g. a temporary network issue, rather than the whole nightly run failing outright

If a job fails after retries, downstream jobs should not run on incomplete or missing data, the pipeline should stop or alert rather than silently produce a wrong report

Mentions monitoring or alerting so someone is notified when a job fails, rather than the team discovering a problem only when the report looks wrong the next day

raw.question: How would you design the scheduling for this set of batch jobs so they run reliably and in the right order?
raw.context: You have three batch jobs that need to run every night: Job A extracts raw order data, Job B transforms it into a cleaned table, and Job C builds a summary report from the cleaned table. Job C must not run until Job B finishes successfully, and Job B must not run until Job A finishes successfully.
